## 464. The real, programmable watchdog built and sim-verified: `watchdog_v1.v`. Real requirement addressed directly, not glossed over: Alan's own explicit point that "the same mechanism could be used in multiple places" means a real, ICM-style cfg_valid-loaded threshold register, not a hardcoded Verilog parameter -- confirmed by actually reconfiguring the SAME instance to a different threshold mid-test and checking it behaves correctly both times. A real testbench bug caught and fixed by debug-tracing rather than guessing, and correctly attributed to the test, not the RTL. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-23)

**STATUS: sim-verified clean, deterministic. Not yet wired into
`dsp_add_wrapper_v1.v` or any real Quartus project.**

**Real design choice, explained not just asserted:** `compare_cell_v1.v`
already has exactly this kind of real, ICM-loaded threshold field
(`cfg_data[39:8]`, confirmed directly from Alan's own real Control
Signals report this session, `#457`). But its own native semantics are
event-driven -- one cardinal arrival, one comparison -- and forcing a
continuously-running counter's live value through that one-shot shape
would need real, awkward glue that doesn't fit the actual use case any
better than a small, dedicated module built for it directly. So
`watchdog_v1.v` keeps the SAME real convention (`cfg_valid` pulse loads
a real register, not a fixed parameter) without forcing reuse where the
existing module's own real semantics don't actually fit -- a real,
stated design choice, not an unexplained divergence.

**Real interface:** `cfg_valid`/`cfg_threshold` (loads a real,
per-instance threshold, same instance reusable anywhere with a
different value each time); `activity_pulse` (whatever the real
"genuine progress happened" signal is at the instantiation site --
for `dsp_add_wrapper_v1.v` that would be `will_fire && ack_in`, a real
operation genuinely completing); `timeout_flag` (held high once
tripped, not a pulse); `count_out` (real live status readback).
Defaults to the maximum representable threshold at reset -- an
unconfigured watchdog never trips prematurely.

**Real test coverage, all passing, deterministic:** never trips before
real configuration; trips at EXACTLY the configured cycle count, not
off-by-one; `activity_pulse` genuinely resets the count before
timeout (a slow-but-progressing chain never trips); **the real point
of this module** -- the SAME instance reconfigured to a DIFFERENT
threshold mid-test, confirmed to trip at the NEW value, not the old
one; `timeout_flag` confirmed to stay held, not pulse.

**A real testbench bug caught and correctly diagnosed, not just
patched:** the first test run showed both timing tests off by exactly
one cycle (5→6, 12→13). Rather than assume the RTL was wrong and
"fix" it to match, added real per-cycle debug tracing with an explicit
settling delay -- confirmed the RTL trips at EXACTLY the right cycle
in every case; the bug was a classic Verilog race condition in the
TEST's own polling loop (reading `timeout_flag` immediately at the
clock edge, before the NBA-scheduled update from that same edge had
settled). Fixed the test, not the RTL, and re-confirmed clean.

**Real, honest scope: not yet integrated.** Wiring `watchdog_v1.v`
into `dsp_add_wrapper_v1.v` (using `will_fire && ack_in` as the real
`activity_pulse`) is the natural next step, not yet done.

## 465. Real watchdog integration complete: `watchdog_v1.v` wired into `dsp_add_wrapper_v1.v`, real threshold exposed as a real wrapper-level port, sim-verified with three new integration tests covering exactly the real failure mode this whole design thread was built to catch. Zero regression on either module's own standalone tests. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-23)

**STATUS: sim-verified clean, deterministic. Not yet a real Quartus
build.**

**A real design decision made explicit, not left implicit:**
`activity_pulse` is defined as ANY genuine forward progress -- either
operand being captured (`ack_out_a`/`ack_out_b`) OR a real operation
completing (`will_fire && ack_in`) -- not just full completion.
Matches `#459`'s own real requirement directly: a chain slowly making
real, partial progress (one operand arrived, still waiting on the
other) must never false-trip a watchdog meant only to catch genuine,
sustained silence.

**The real threshold is a real wrapper-level port
(`wd_cfg_valid`/`wd_cfg_threshold`), not buried or hardcoded** -- the
actual integrator decides the real value for the real context this
specific instance sits in, matching Alan's own explicit requirement
that the same mechanism stay reusable with a different threshold per
instantiation.

**Three new real integration tests, all passing, covering the exact
real failure mode this design thread exists to catch:**
1. Normal real operation (both operands arrive, real op completes)
   never false-trips a reasonably-set watchdog.
2. Genuine, sustained silence (nothing offered at all) DOES trip it,
   at exactly the configured cycle count.
3. **The real point:** partial progress -- just one operand arriving,
   no full operation ever completing -- correctly resets the count,
   confirming a slow-but-genuinely-progressing chain is never mistaken
   for a stuck one.

**Zero regression:** both `dsp_add_wrapper_v1.v`'s own original
protocol tests (dual-operand capture, both arrival orders, held-fire,
re-arming) and `watchdog_v1.v`'s own standalone tests re-run unchanged
and still pass.

**Real, honest scope: what's still open.** No real Quartus project
exists for this wrapper yet. The real `alterafpf_add_single` megafunction
still needs generating via IP Catalog and its exact port names
confirming (`#462`'s own stated gap). No real hardware test yet --
same "build now, confirm against real generation" pattern as every
other real IP integration this session.

Two real, honest findings discovered from this real run, neither glossed over: (1) the real IP chosen does NOT use hard DSP silicon at all -- a genuine, unexpected correction to this project's own original premise; (2) the one real test failure is a real test-design mismatch, not a watchdog bug -- traced precisely, not just re-labeled. **Real success, confirmed on actual silicon, not sim:** Flow Status
Successful, 568 ALM, 158.88 MHz on `clk_div` (real, comfortable margin
over the 25MHz target). Real operation 1 (A=0xAAAA0001, B=0x55550002):
fire correctly asserted, result read back, matching the real stub's
own deterministic (non-IEEE754) test pattern exactly. Real ACK
correctly cleared fire. Real operation 2 confirmed the wrapper
genuinely re-arms for a second real operation. `#471`'s own real,
twice-corrected entity name and port list are now confirmed CORRECT
against real silicon, not just sim.

**Real, honest finding #1 -- this project's own original premise about
"free" hardware acceleration needs correcting, not defended:**
`Total DSP Blocks 0 / 1,687` in the real Fitter summary. The real
Control Signals data shows genuine internal floating-point datapath
logic (`FPAddSub|...alignmentShifter...`, real IEEE-754 mantissa-
alignment machinery) built entirely from fabric LUTs/ALMs -- the
"Floating Point Hardware 2 Multi-cycle" IP (the Nios II Custom
Instruction variant this project has been using since `#469`) is a
real, confirmed SOFT implementation, not hardware-accelerated via real
DSP blocks at all. This directly corrects `#453`/`#461`'s own original
framing ("the DSP does the math side completely... no real change to
the cell, no fabric cost") -- real, honest, now-known-wrong for THIS
specific IP choice. The real alternative that likely DOES use hard DSP
silicon -- "Native Floating Point DSP Intel Arria 10 FPGA IP" under
Primitive DSP -- was seen in the real IP Catalog browse (Alan's own
earlier screenshot) but not the one chosen. Real, open question for a
future session: is real hard-DSP offload still the goal, and if so,
does that alternative IP need investigating instead.

**Real, honest finding #2 -- the ONE real test failure, traced
precisely, not just re-labeled a bug:** "FAIL: watchdog false-tripped"
during real operation 1. Real, precise diagnosis, not assumed: the
VERY FIRST real status read (before any command was even sent) already
showed `wd_timeout_err=1, wd_count=65535` -- the watchdog's own
default 16-bit ceiling (65,535 cycles = 2.62ms at the real 25MHz
operating frequency), already reached before the test script's own
first real JTAG interaction completed. This is NOT a watchdog bug --
real JTAG round-trip overhead genuinely exceeds 2.62ms (matching
`#448`'s own already-measured real figure, ~6.5ms/command). When the
test then set a real threshold of 50 cycles (2 real microseconds,
copied directly from the fast-simulation testbench value) the watchdog
correctly tripped again, since no real JTAG command can possibly
arrive within 2 microseconds -- confirmed precisely: the real JTAG
inter-command gap (`#448`: ~162,500 cycles) is roughly **3,250x larger**
than the 50-cycle threshold the test actually used. The watchdog did
exactly what it was designed to do; the test threshold was sized for
simulation speed, not real hardware timescales -- a real, useful,
concrete finding from actual hardware testing, not something that
could have been caught in sim alone (since the sim stub's own
simulated JTAG round-trip has no real timing cost).

**Real, honest scope for next session -- two real, separate follow-up
items, neither urgent, neither blocking the real, core success
already achieved:**
1. Real, sensible watchdog thresholds for JTAG-host-driven testing need
   to be chosen with `#448`'s own real ~6.5ms/command figure in mind
   (or wider still, for real margin) -- NOT the tiny values convenient
   for fast simulation. A real, wider `WATCHDOG_WIDTH` (24 or 32 bits)
   would also give more real headroom before hitting the default
   ceiling during normal JTAG-paced use.
2. Whether to pursue the real, hard-DSP-block-using IP alternative

- Real ISSP IP: 89.7 ALM

568** -- the earlier 568 figure included the one-time, shared JTAG
bridge + ISSP + SLD debug infrastructure (199.2 ALM combined), which a
larger design with many DSP instances would only pay ONCE, not per
instance. Re-run of the 27-chain baseline: 27 x 354.0 = 9,558 ALM,
**3.80% of total fabric** (not the earlier 6.09% estimate using the
inflated 568 figure).

from the previous exchange:** the real float-add core (299.5 ALM) is
the dominant real cost, ~85% of the whole wrapper's own total -- this

(51.8+23.7=75.5 ALM combined, ~21% of the wrapper). Confirms directly
that IF a soft-logic float core became a real, new `core_select`
option inside `unicell_super_v1` (per the earlier real discussion),

## 479. Real, final, five-tool pipeline architecture agreed -- the whole real design-tooling picture this project needs, clarified precisely after several real naming collisions were caught and corrected in conversation rather than left ambiguous. Nothing built. A real, complete architectural map for the whole future design/build/program/inspect flow. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**Real, final architecture, each tool's own real input/output stated
precisely, no ambiguity remaining:**

| Tool | Real input | Real output | Real dependency |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Composer** | Real, chosen element set (from a real element library, `#478`'s own item C1) | Real `top.v` files, ready for a real Quartus build into a `.sof` | Needs the real **MAN** file (device/board facts) only |
| **Compiler** | A real program (DSL/Python-AST) referencing built-in tiles and/or the user's own library | A real **ICM** file | Needs a real **SHAPE** file (to check the design fits/routes against real constraints) and the real **user tile library** |
| **Walker** | A real, already-built `.sof`, ALREADY WRITTEN to a real card | A real **SHAPE** file (the actual, real, as-built mapping) | Runs strictly AFTER real hardware programming -- cannot run before |
| **VM** | Either a real SHAPE file (mirror mode), or nothing (free mode) | A live, running instance the user can program against | **Mirror mode**: needs a real SHAPE file (reflects an actual card's real constraints). **Free mode**: no file needed -- an unconstrained, arbitrary-scale matrix (spawn 10,000 cells, no real hardware limit) |
| **Tile Designer** | A user's own visual model design | A real ICM file, same format as any built-in Tier-0/Tier-1 tile, usable in either VM mode | Reuses the real, already-found-reusable visual paradigm from the OLD archived Composer (`#387`'s own real finding: canvas/drag-link/library-panel reusable, data model was not) -- but as its OWN tool, not folded back into "Composer," to avoid exactly the naming collision this conversation just had to untangle |

**Real, important structural facts, confirmed precisely, not
approximated:**
- Composer and Walker are the only two tools that ever touch real
  hardware/Quartus directly. Compiler and VM (both modes) operate
  entirely on already-produced files (MAN/SHAPE/ICM) -- genuinely
  software-only, no real build in their own critical path.
- SHAPE is the real, central connective artifact: produced by ONE tool
  (Walker) and consumed by TWO others (Compiler, VM mirror mode) --
  the same real, as-built card data feeding both "does my program fit"
  and "what does the card actually look like right now."
- The real, inherent ordering constraint: Composer -> real Quartus
  build -> Walker -> (Compiler targeting that real card) OR (VM in
  mirror mode). VM free mode and Tile Designer output have NO real
  hardware dependency at all and can be built/used independent of
  everything else in this chain.

**Real, honest scope: nothing built. This entry is the complete,
agreed architectural map only** -- see `#478`'s own itemized real gap
list for what's actually needed to build each piece, now correctly
attributed to the right tool given this session's own real naming
corrections.

## 480. Real, first piece of #479's own agreed VM-first priority order: DspWrapperCell built for the VM free-mode path -- real IEEE-754 correctness (genuinely better than the RTL sim stubs, which deliberately don't do real math), real two-port capture protocol matching the hardware-confirmed RTL, and real, working integration into the existing SuperGrid tick loop with zero changes to that engine. Two real bugs caught by actually running the test, not assumed correct. Zero regression on the full existing 29-test VM suite. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: real, tested, working. First concrete step on #479's own
agreed "VM extensions first, no real hardware dependency" priority.**

**Real, deliberate architectural choice, not an oversight:**
`DspWrapperCell` is a genuinely SEPARATE class, not a new `core` value
inside `SuperCell`. Matches the real, already-agreed hardware
architecture (`#453`/`#474`): DSP wrappers are dedicated, placement-
anchored infrastructure, explicitly NOT part of the super carrier
shell's own `core_select` mux. Keeping that same distinction in the VM
even in unconstrained free mode avoids creating a real inconsistency
for the future mirror mode, which DOES need to honestly reflect a real
card's own placement-constrained DSP wrappers.

**A real improvement over the RTL simulation stubs, not just parity:**
the real Quartus sim stubs (`tb_stub_alterafpf_*_v1.v`) deliberately
skip real IEEE-754 arithmetic -- verifying the RTL's own protocol
timing was the point, not reimplementing a float unit in a testbench.
This VM class has no such constraint: Python's own `struct` module
gives genuine, correct IEEE-754 single-precision arithmetic directly --
this is actually MORE correct than the RTL testbenches for the real
computed value, matching this whole VM's own stated design philosophy
("correctness of protocol, ordering, and computed results, not cycle-
for-cycle timing").

**Real interface, duck-typed to match `SuperGrid.tick()`'s own real,
existing expectations exactly** (`deliver()`, `_offer_state()`,
`is_continuously_live()`, `clear_valid_on_drain()`, `pending_ack`,
`addon_config`) -- ZERO changes needed to `SuperGrid`/`SuperCell`'s own
real, existing code to support it sitting in the same live grid
alongside ordinary cells.

**Two real bugs caught by actually running the test, not assumed
correct from reading the code:**
1. First draft's own capture-gating logic was needlessly convoluted
   (redundant conditions) -- simplified and re-verified.
2. `AttributeError: 'DspWrapperCell' object has no attribute
   'addon_config'` -- the grid's own generic offer pass assumes every
   cell has this field. Real, honest fix: an empty dict is a correct
   no-op through `apply_addons()`, not a workaround -- DSP wrappers
   genuinely have no real ADDON wrapping in the current architecture.
3. The real grid-integration test itself initially failed (`result=
   None`) -- traced precisely rather than assumed a class bug: the
   test only called `tick()` once, but an offered value becomes
   pending for the NEXT tick, not processed within the same one --
   matching how every other single-shot core in this VM already
   works. Fixed the test, not the class, after confirming the class's
   own real behavior was correct.

**Real test coverage, all passing, deterministic:** genuine IEEE-754
correctness for ADD/SUB/MUL/GE; both operand-arrival orders (A-first
and B-first); real re-arm after a drain; safe no-op on `injected`
(the real RTL has no such path either, only real cardinal a/b
arrivals); full, real integration into a live `SuperGrid` alongside an
ordinary `SuperCell`, offering a real computed value that the RAM cell
correctly receives two ticks later.

**Real, honest scope -- what's NOT modeled, stated plainly, not
glossed over:** real per-operation cycle latency (5/5/4/1/1/0 cycles,
`#469`) is not modeled -- consistent with this whole VM's own event-
driven, not cycle-accurate, abstraction level (same choice already
made for every other core). The real watchdog's own timeout behavior
is also not modeled -- `#472`'s own real finding (thresholds are
meaningless without real JTAG-paced-vs-fabric-internal wall-clock
time) has no clean analog in a tick-counted, hardware-free VM; a real,
separate future decision, not assumed here.

## 481. Real watchdog added to DspWrapperCell -- second piece of #479's own agreed VM-first priority. Honestly re-based to VM tick-counting rather than real hardware cycles, with the real protective purpose (#464's own design) fully preserved. All real tests pass on the first run -- no bugs found this time, a real, clean build. Zero regression. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: real, tested, working. Second concrete step on #479's own
agreed VM-first priority order.**

**A real, honest design decision, stated precisely, not glossed over:**
the watchdog now counts VM TICKS of inactivity, not real hardware
clock cycles. `#472`'s own real finding (a threshold sized for
simulation false-trips against real, JTAG-paced hardware) doesn't
disappear just because this is a hardware-free VM -- but the real
PROTECTIVE PURPOSE (catch genuine, sustained inactivity; never trip on
real, ongoing progress) transfers cleanly to tick-counting even though
the specific number has no real hardware-cycle meaning. `watchdog_
tick()` is an explicit, separate call the driver makes once per real
grid tick -- NOT auto-invoked by `SuperGrid.tick()`, which stays
completely untouched, same real discipline as `#480`'s own original
design choice.

**Real activity definition ported faithfully from the real RTL
(`#465`):** ANY genuine new capture (`ack_out_a`/`ack_out_b`
equivalent) OR a real drain (`will_fire && ack_in` equivalent) resets
the count -- not just full operation completion. Implemented by
comparing `_primed_a`/`_primed_b` state before and after each real
`deliver()` call, and marking activity explicitly in `clear_valid_on_
drain()`.

**Real, programmable design ported faithfully from `#464`:**
`configure_watchdog(threshold)` -- `None` disables it (never trips,
matching the real RTL's own unconfigured-default behavior),
reconfiguring also resets any in-flight count, matching the real
hardware's own `cfg_valid` behavior exactly.

**Real test coverage, all passing, deterministic, genuinely clean --
no bugs found and fixed this time, unlike `#480`'s own two real
catches:** disabled by default, never trips even after 1000 ticks;
trips at EXACTLY the configured tick count (10), not off-by-one; real
partial progress (one operand arriving, no full pair) correctly resets
the count, matching `#459`'s own real "patient, don't false-trip on
real progress" requirement; normal operation (both operands, real
drain) never false-trips a reasonably-set threshold; the real point of
the whole design -- the SAME instance reconfigured to a DIFFERENT
threshold (5 -> 15) trips correctly at the new value, not the old one.

**Real, honest scope -- what's still open:** ICM-level construction
(building a `DspWrapperCell` from a real program/ICM file rather than
only direct Python calls) remains unbuilt -- `#478`'s own real
compiler-gap item 4 (named-library lookup, DSL syntax for operation
selection) is a separate, larger, not-yet-started piece.

## 482. Real checkpoint/freeze/save/wipe/reload built and tested for DspWrapperCell -- a real model (two chained DSP wrapper cells, built via direct Python calls), driven into genuine mid-flight state, frozen, saved, the Python objects actually deleted, reloaded, and confirmed both DATA-exact and FUNCTIONALLY correct on continuation. Real tamper detection confirmed too, reusing the exact discipline already established for ICM files. One real bug caught and fixed (a missing import), zero regression. Third real piece of #479's own VM-first priority. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: real, tested, working. Third concrete step on #479's own
agreed VM-first priority order.**

**Real, deliberate scope decision, stated precisely:** this checkpoints
DspWrapperCell specifically, not a full mixed grid including SuperCell
-- a real, separate, larger task, not attempted in this pass. The
saved format (`(row,col) -> cell` dict) deliberately mirrors
`SuperGrid.cells`'s own real shape so it can extend later without a
format change.

**Real, honest reasoning on scope, not glossed over:** this project's
own established checkpoint principle for real hardware ("cell states
yes, DSP states no" -- a real hard-DSP block's own internal pipeline
state is never captured, only drained-and-settled cell state) doesn't
directly transfer here in the same form, because `DspWrapperCell`
(`#480`'s own stated scope) has no real multi-cycle pipeline to model
in the first place -- a captured operand pair resolves to a result
within the SAME `deliver()` call. So the honest scope here is simpler
and complete: every field affecting future behavior is captured,
nothing silently dropped.

**Real, genuine mid-flight test, not a clean quiescent snapshot:** the
real model was driven into an actually in-progress, unresolved state
before freezing -- one cell with only operand A captured (not a full
pair), the other holding an undrained real result, both watchdogs at
real nonzero counts. This is deliberately harder than checkpointing a
settled state, and it's the real, honest test of whether the mechanism
actually works.

**Real wipe, not a stale reference:** `del add_cell, mul_cell` plus an
explicit `gc.collect()` -- the objects genuinely no longer exist in
memory before reload, not merely reassigned.

**Real, dual confirmation after reload, not just a data comparison:**
every captured field matches exactly (config, mid-flight capture
state, held result, watchdog count) AND the reloaded cell was then
DRIVEN further (fed its still-missing operand) and produced the
correct real computed result (3.5+1.5=5.0) -- confirming the reloaded
object is functionally live and correct, not merely a faithful data
snapshot that happens to look right.

**Real tamper detection confirmed, reusing an already-established
discipline, not invented fresh:** same JSON + SHA-256 hash-
verification pattern already proven for `icm_v3.IcmV3File` (`nano/
icm_v3.py`) -- a hand-edited saved file is correctly rejected with a
clear error, not silently loaded wrong.

**One real bug caught and fixed:** first test run failed with
`NameError: name 'save_model' is not defined` -- a genuinely missing
import in the test file, not a bug in the checkpoint mechanism itself.
Fixed directly, re-confirmed clean.

**Real test coverage, all passing, deterministic:** pre-freeze
mid-flight state confirmed real; every field exact-matches after
reload; real functional continuation produces the correct computed
result; real tamper detection via hash mismatch.

**Real, honest scope for what's still open:** full mixed-grid
checkpointing (SuperCell + DspWrapperCell together) remains a real,
separate, not-yet-built task. ICM-level construction (building a model
from a real program/DSL rather than only direct Python calls) also
remains open, per `#478`'s own compiler-gap item 4.

## 483. Full mixed-grid checkpointing built and tested -- SuperCell.checkpoint()/restore() (generic, dataclass-driven, all ~30 fields across all 6 cores + delegated nano CACell) plus nano/mixed_grid_checkpoint_v1.py (save_mixed_model/load_mixed_model, tagged cell_class dispatch to SuperCell or DspWrapperCell). Real, genuine mixed mid-flight state (dsp/adder both half-fed, accumulator mid-count) checkpointed together, wiped, reloaded, and confirmed both data-exact and functionally correct through a real, live SuperGrid.tick() propagation, not just isolated field comparison. Zero regression, 285/285 (was 283). (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: real, tested, working. Closes #482's own explicitly-flagged "full mixed-grid checkpointing" gap -- Alan's own choice of which paused thread to pick back up.**

**Real, deliberate design choice on SuperCell -- generic over hand-typed, unlike #480's own DspWrapperCell:** `SuperCell` carries ~30 real fields spanning all 6 cores' own register sets (every core is always physically present per #159's own docstring, only the selected one is ever written). A hand-typed field list here would be real, ongoing field-drift risk every time a core gains a field -- so `checkpoint()`/`restore()` use `dataclasses.fields()` introspection instead, the same "generic over hand-typed" principle this codebase already committed to for ICM field tables (#356's `generic_field_codec_v1.py`, proven bit-for-bit equivalent to `icm_v3.py`'s own hand-typed one). `_nano` is the one real special case, handled separately: a nested `CACell` dataclass gets its own real `dataclasses.asdict()`/reconstruction rather than being swept into the generic per-field loop.

**Real, honest test discipline, two layers:** first, `SuperCell.checkpoint()`/`restore()` proven ALONE, in isolation, across three genuinely different core types (adder mid-flight A-only, accumulator with a real nonzero running total, nano with a delegated CACell driven into real non-default state -- `a_data`/`a_arrived`/`pending_ack` all distinguishing values) -- before trusting the mixed-grid layer built on top. Second, the real, full task: a genuine three-cell mixed chain (`DspWrapperCell` -> `SuperCell` adder -> `SuperCell` accumulator, real downstream masks wiring them together) driven into real, simultaneously mid-flight state for ALL THREE cells at once (dsp has only operand A, adder has only operand A, accumulator sits mid-count at 3) -- checkpointed together as ONE file, wiped (real `del` + `gc.collect()`), reloaded, and then actually run FURTHER: both half-fed cells resolved with their missing operand, and the adder's now-ready offer propagated through two real `SuperGrid.tick()` calls into the accumulator, confirming the reconstructed chain's WIRING survived reload, not just each cell's own isolated field values.

**Real, deliberate design choice on the mixed-grid file format:** a single `cell_class` discriminator tag ("super" | "dsp_wrapper") per snapshot, dispatching to each class's own already-proven `checkpoint()`/`restore()` unmodified -- neither `SuperCell` nor `DspWrapperCell` needed to change to support living in the same checkpoint file. Same real SHA-256 hash-verification discipline as `IcmV3File` and `#480`'s own `save_model`/`load_model`, confirmed via the same real tamper test (hand-edited saved JSON correctly rejected, not silently loaded wrong).

**Real test coverage, all passing:** `tests/vm/test_mixed_grid_checkpoint_v1.py`, two functions -- isolated `SuperCell` round-trip (adder/accumulator/nano, each with real functional continuation after restore, not just a data match), and the full mixed-grid freeze/wipe/reload/continue/tamper-detect test. Zero bugs found this pass (unlike #480's one real missing-import catch) -- the generic dataclass-introspection approach worked correctly on the first real run.

**Real, honest scope for what's still open:** ICM-level construction (building a model, including DSP wrapper cells, from a real program/DSL rather than only direct Python calls) remains unbuilt -- `#478`'s own compiler-gap item 4, unchanged. This entry closes the OTHER of #482's two flagged next pieces.

## 484. Real, new ICM v4 format built -- a genuine mixed-cell file format (SUPER_LATCH super-cell records, unchanged from ICM v3, alongside a new real DspWrapperRecord kind), constructed directly via Python (no DSL/compiler stage -- the compiler doesn't know DSP wrappers exist yet, a real, separate, not-yet-started upgrade). Built, saved, hash-verified on load (spanning BOTH record kinds), tamper-detected on either side, and driven through a real live SuperGrid built directly from the file to confirm a genuine DSP-wrapper-ADD-into-RAM-sink program computes the correct result end to end. Zero regression, 291/291 (was 285). (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: real, tested, working. This is the ICM-level-construction piece #478/#482 both flagged open -- built explicitly WITHOUT the compiler, per Alan's own direct instruction, since the compiler's own tile library/resolver doesn't know DSP wrappers exist at all yet (a real, separate, documented gap -- `dsp_wrapper_timing.md`'s own "what's still open" item 1).**

**Real, deliberate reason for a NEW format number (`icm-v4`), not a silent extension of `icm-v3`:** DSP wrapper cells are a real, deliberate, SEPARATE hardware class from `unicell_super_v1.v` (`#453`/`#474` -- dedicated, placement-anchored infrastructure, never a `core_select` option). A file naming both kinds is a genuinely new capability an ICM v3 reader has no `SEL_*` for -- silently tolerating that would be exactly the kind of unnoticed-drop risk `icm_v3.py`'s own `_pack_fields()` already refuses elsewhere (unknown field names are a hard error, not a silent `.get(..., 0)`). A real, explicit `format_version="icm-v4"` makes the incompatibility checkable on load rather than hoped-past.

**Real, honest reuse, not reinvention:** `IcmV4File.super_records` is a plain list of ICM v3's own `IcmV3Record`, used completely unmodified -- `icm_v3.py` itself was not touched. `DspWrapperRecord` is the one genuinely new record kind, matching `DspWrapperCell`'s own real constructor shape (`op`/`a_dir`/`b_dir`/`downstream_mask`/optional `watchdog_threshold`) -- deliberately STATIC CONFIGURATION only, the same category as a super cell's own `core_config`, not runtime state (that split -- config file vs. runtime checkpoint -- already exists for the super/DSP-wrapper pair via `icm_v3.IcmV3File` vs. `dsp_wrapper_automaton_v1.save_model`, and this keeps the same shape rather than blurring it).

**`build_grid()` -- the honest current substitute for a real loader/binder stage, stated plainly as such in the module's own docstring:** turns a saved ICM v4 file directly into a live `SuperGrid`, keyed `(row, col)` exactly like `mixed_grid_checkpoint_v1.py`'s own established convention, dispatching each record to `SuperCell.from_record()` or the new `DspWrapperRecord.build_cell()`. A real, explicit position-collision check (two records claiming the same cell is a hard `ValueError`, not silently resolved by load order) -- caught by its own dedicated test, not assumed safe.

**Real test coverage, `tests/vm/test_icm_v4.py`, 6 functions, all passing first run, zero bugs found:** record round-trip, unknown-op rejection, `build_cell()` producing behaviorally-identical results to direct construction (real SUB computed and compared, not just config fields), full save/load/hash-verify (BOTH a tampered DSP field and a tampered super-record field independently confirmed caught by the one combined hash, not just one side), and the real point of the whole format -- a saved DSP-wrapper-ADD-into-RAM-sink program loaded and run through two real `SuperGrid.tick()` calls, correct real IEEE-754 result (2.5+1.5=4.0) confirmed arriving at the RAM sink.

**Real, honest scope for what's still open:** the DSL/compiler upgrade itself (teaching the tile library and resolver that DSP wrappers exist, so a real Unicell-S program could target this format instead of direct Python calls) remains real, separate, unbuilt work -- explicitly out of scope for this entry, per Alan's own instruction. A real Tile Designer / placement-anchoring story for DSP wrappers specifically (per `#476`'s own open items 2-5) is also still open.

## 485. Real, generic compiler hook built -- tile_source_registry_v1.py, plus a new DSP-wrapper model library (dsp_wrapper_tile_library_v1.py) that self-registers into it -- lets the compiler resolve a DSP wrapper tile by name exactly like any super tile, with zero DSP-wrapper-specific code added to dsl_compiler_v1.py's own resolve/place/emit control flow. A real DSL program placing a DSP wrapper tile alongside an ordinary super tile now compiles end to end (through the SAME unmodified compile_source() entry point) into a real, new IcmV4File; a program using no DSP wrapper tiles produces the exact same IcmV3File as before -- confirmed backward-compatible, not just assumed. Zero regression, 301/301 (was 291). (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: real, tested, working. This is the real "hook, not rewrite" extension mechanism Alan asked for directly -- a new tile library registers itself; the compiler never learns a new kind's name.**

**Real, deliberate architecture -- three real pieces:**
1. `nano/tile_source_registry_v1.py` -- a tiny, deliberately narrow registry: a `TileSource` bundles a library (`names()`/`get()`), a `place_fn` matching the real, established `place(tile, row, col, port_directions, params, cell_id=...) -> record` shape every Tier-0 `place()` function already uses, and a `bucket` name (which real output list -- `super_records`/`dsp_wrapper_records` -- a resolved record belongs in). `find_source_for()`/`all_known_tile_names()` are the only two things the compiler ever calls.
2. `nano/dsp_wrapper_tile_library_v1.py` -- a real, dedicated Tier-0-shaped tile library for the DSP wrapper family (`dsp_add`/`dsp_sub`/`dsp_mul`/`dsp_ge`/`dsp_le`/`dsp_neq`, one per real confirmed op, `dsp_add` marked `proven="silicon-proven"` per `#472`, the rest `sim-only`), targeting `icm_v4.DspWrapperRecord`. Deliberately NOT built by reusing `super_tile_library_v1.py`'s own generic field-grouping resolver -- DSP wrapper's real `a_dir`/`b_dir` are genuinely single, distinct cardinal directions (never a fan-out dirmask the way `downstream_mask`/`upstream_mask` are on every super-cell core), so a small, honest, parallel resolver was the more correct choice than bolting a special case onto an already-proven module. Self-registers into the registry at its own import time.
3. `super_tile_library_v1.py` -- one small, additive, real change: it now ALSO self-registers into the same registry (proving the hook covers what already worked, not just the new kind it was built alongside). Zero behavior change for anything already calling `super_tile_library`/`place()` directly.

**`dsl_compiler_v1.py`'s own real changes, all generalizations, none DSP-wrapper-specific:** `_resolve_and_place()` now asks `find_source_for()` instead of hardcoding `super_tile_library`, and returns `{bucket_name: [record,...]}` instead of a flat list; `compile_program_ir()`'s consuming loop buckets records generically by name; `_param_names()` now checks `hasattr(tile, "param_names")` instead of `isinstance(tile, SuperTileSpec)`, so it works for any future Tier-0-shaped tile class without edits. The one place the file still names a kind explicitly is its own import block -- `import dsp_wrapper_tile_library_v1` for the self-registration side effect -- documented plainly as "the one line a future tile-kind module needs added here," an honest, minimal, unavoidable consequence of Python's own import model, not a gap in the design.

**Real, deliberate backward-compatible output selection:** `compile_program_ir()`/`compile_source()` return the exact same real `v3.IcmV3File` as always when a program places no DSP wrapper tile (confirmed directly, not assumed, by a dedicated test asserting `isinstance(icm, v3.IcmV3File)` and NOT `IcmV4File`) -- only a program that DOES place at least one DSP wrapper tile produces the new `v4.IcmV4File`. Mirrors `#484`'s own "new format number, not a silent extension" discipline, applied here to output SELECTION rather than format definition.

**Real, honest scope, stated plainly, not silently half-supported:** Tier-1 composed tiles (`define`/`place_composed()`) remain super-tile-only sub-cells -- `place_composed()` itself still only knows how to emit `IcmV3Record`s, so a `define` block cannot yet mix a DSP wrapper primitive in as a sub-cell. `_resolve_tile_by_name()`/`_process_define()` were deliberately left untouched (still reference `super_tile_library` directly) to avoid a half-working, confusing capability with an obscure failure deep inside `place_composed()` -- extending composed tiles to multiple record kinds is real, separate, future work.

**Real test coverage, `tests/vm/test_dsp_wrapper_tile_library_v1.py`, 10 functions, one real bug caught and fixed in the TEST itself (not the library) -- comparing an unpacked direction list against a packed int, fixed by checking `to_dict()`'s own packed output instead:** direct `DspWrapperTileSpec`/`place()` correctness (real record produced, same-direction rejection, list-for-single-port rejection, real fan-out on `out`, optional watchdog passthrough); the registry itself (`find_source_for()` returns the right bucket for both kinds, unknown names return `None`, `all_known_tile_names()` spans both); and the real point of the whole entry -- a super-only program proven byte-for-byte backward compatible, PLUS a real mixed DSL program (`dsp_add` feeding a `ram_flowing` sink) compiled end to end into `IcmV4File`, saved, reloaded, and run through a real live `SuperGrid.tick()` pair, correct IEEE-754 result (1.25+2.75=4.0) confirmed. The unknown-tile error path was also confirmed to now list DSP wrapper names in its suggestion, proving the generalization reaches the error path too, not just the happy path.

**Real, honest scope for what's still open:** composed-tile (Tier-1) support for non-super tile kinds; a Tile Designer or DSL syntax specifically for choosing among registered kinds beyond plain `place NAME as TILE_NAME`; extending the pattern to any future dedicated hardware class beyond DSP wrappers (the registry itself needs no changes to do so -- a new library module + one import line in `dsl_compiler_v1.py` is the whole integration cost, per this entry's own real design).

**Real, deliberate scoping choice, written down BEFORE any code (`docs/stripped-cell/design-notes/tile_designer_scope.md`):** the old archived Composer's own real finding (`#387`) was "visual paradigm reusable, data model not" -- checked again here, and one further real correction made: the old tool's "drag from output port, release on input port" gesture assumed BUS addressing (any cell to any cell). Unicell-S has no such freedom -- every real link is a chosen CARDINAL DIRECTION, meaningful only with a real physically-adjacent neighbor (`_OPPOSITE` convention). The Tile Designer's own real link gesture is therefore "select an instance, choose a direction per port" -- a genuinely corrected paradigm, not a lesser one, because it's what the hardware actually does.

Fixed the same way `dsl_compiler_v1.py` already does it -- explicit `# noqa: F401` imports of both library modules, documented as "the one line a future tile-kind module needs added here," now confirmed true a second time in a second consuming file.

**Real test coverage, `tests/vm/test_tile_designer_v1.py`, 17 functions, all passing, mirroring `test_workbench_v1.py`'s own two-layer discipline:** controller-only tests (unknown tile/duplicate id/unknown port rejection, move/remove, unresolved-port validation failure, real position-collision detection, a composed `sentinel` instance placed through the Designer, `save_icm()` producing a real reloadable file); the real point -- a mixed DSP-wrapper + super-cell design exported to `IcmV4File` and run through an actual live `SuperGrid`, correct real result (2.0+5.5=7.5) confirmed; and a real, running HTTP server (real sockets, real `urllib` requests) exercised through the identical full sequence -- add/wire/validate/export -- confirming the HTTP layer, not just the controller in isolation.

**Real, deliberate design choice: connection status lives server-side, not in JS.** `TileDesignerController._port_connections()` computes, per wired port, the real target cell `(row, col)` for its chosen direction and whether a real neighboring instance sits there (`"connected"`) or not (`"open"`) -- returned as part of `/describe`'s own response. This mirrors the project's own long-standing principle (config/validation logic belongs in one authoritative, testable place, not duplicated into an unverifiable client) and means the ONLY new server-side surface is a pure geometric lookup against already-existing state, not a second copy of any real port/param validation (`place()`/`place_composed()` remain the sole authority for THAT, unchanged).

**Real, honest note on composed-tile indicators, stated plainly in the code itself:** `_port_connections()` computes from the instance's own anchor `(row, col)` -- exact for every Tier-0-shaped tile (whose anchor IS its one real cell), but an approximation for a composed (Tier-1) instance, whose real ports may belong to a sub-cell offset from the anchor (`#486`). The underlying export via `place()`/`place_composed()` is completely unaffected either way -- this only concerns how the indicator is DRAWN, not what gets exported. Not fixed here -- correctly attributing indicators to a composed tile's own real sub-cell footprint is real, separate, future work, not silently claimed as solved.

**Real drag gesture, matching `tile_designer_scope.md`'s own corrected paradigm exactly:** drag FROM an occupied grid cell (the source instance), drop on an immediately-adjacent cell -- the real cardinal direction is inferred from the drop geometry (`directionFromDelta()`), then whichever of the source's own still-unwired ports applies gets set to it via the SAME existing `/set_port` endpoint (no new REST surface needed for this). Ambiguity (more than one unwired port) prompts for which one by name rather than guessing. A non-adjacent or diagonal drop is rejected with a real, honest message, not silently ignored.

**Real, proven-where-provable test coverage, `tests/vm/test_tile_designer_v1.py`, 5 new functions (22 total in the file), zero regression, 327/327 (was 322):** direct Python tests confirm `/describe`'s own connection reporting -- open vs. connected status, correct target coordinates, fan-out ports reporting a real list of connections (one per direction), and unwired ports reporting no connection entry at all; the real mixed end-to-end HTTP server test extended to also check `/describe`'s own connection status over real sockets, not just the controller in isolation; and a genuinely new testing approach for this codebase -- `directionFromDelta()`/`unwiredPorts()` extracted directly from the served HTML and run through a real `node` subprocess (skips cleanly if `node` isn't available, doesn't fail the suite over an environment gap), confirming all four real cardinal cases, the self-drop/diagonal/two-step rejection cases, and both empty and populated unwired-port-list cases.

**Real, honest scope for what's still open, per Alan's own stated next steps:** a short, stepped onboarding flow through the Designer; a real, explicit "data input point" concept -- an OPEN connection edge deliberately marked as a boundary injection point rather than left ambiguous, tying directly into the `"open"` status this entry's own connection reporting already surfaces. Neither started here.

## 491. Real, important architectural realization, Alan's own words, captured precisely before session close: the branching capability (`dynamic_route_en`/`pattern_low`/`pattern_equal`/`pattern_high`, confirmed real and still present but fenced off from the super shell, `#490`'s own answer) should be promoted INTO the super cell -- even as a core extra -- not left stranded on the nano-only path. Without it, the whole system degrades to a strictly linear, serial chain with no runtime branching anywhere -- Alan's own diagnosis for why the current scope has felt small: it's not that less is possible, it's that a specific, small set of real bits (branching, and by the same logic the rest of nano's "full" feature set -- hold/feedback/command-cell) never made the jump from the standalone nano cell into the super carrier shell. A real, second observation in the same breath: the FULL cell (the original, archived architecture) was in some concrete ways MORE flexible than the current stripped/nano-based super cell precisely because of small capabilities like this one that didn't carry forward in the pivot -- not a blanket claim the full cell was better, a precise one about which specific bits made the difference. (Alan, 2026-08-24)

**STATUS: a real, unbuilt architectural direction, captured precisely for next session -- nothing scoped into concrete steps yet, matching this project's own standing discipline of logging a real decision before it drifts, especially at a deliberate stopping point.**

**The real, precise shape of the gap, per `#490`'s own direct finding:** `unicell_super_v1.v`'s own nano-core reconstruction (its `core_select=0` case) wires through only the "basic" subset of the standalone nano cell (`unicell_stripped_v1.v`) -- `topology`/`ready`/`routing_mask`/`cardinal_edge`. Everything else the real, full nano cell can do -- `dynamic_route_en`'s own comparator-driven branching (`pattern_low`/`pattern_equal`/`pattern_high`, `#140`/`#156`), `hold_in`/`fb_internal_in` (continuous internal feedback, `#118`), `is_command_cell` (multi-opcode programming, `#123`) -- was never wired into the super shell at all. `super_tile_library_v1.py` already names this exact boundary as a real, reserved-but-unbuilt `target="nano-full"` tag, "aspirational, not yet usable," because no standalone Unicell-n ICM format exists to build such a tile against.

**The real, structural consequence Alan named directly:** without branching reachable from ANY super-cell tile, every program built through the current tile libraries/DSL/Tile Designer is necessarily a strictly linear, serial pipeline -- data flows one direction through a fixed chain of cells, with no cell able to choose which of several downstream paths a value takes based on the value itself. Alan's own diagnosis: this is a real, concrete reason the current architecture's own scope has felt smaller than intended -- not a broad complaint, a precise identification of which specific missing capability produces that feeling.

**The real, second, related observation:** the original FULL cell (`unicell64_v3.v`, archived to `archeology/full-cell/` when the project pivoted to the stripped/nano cell) had this branching capability -- and by the same reasoning, the rest of nano's full feature set -- genuinely available, in a way the current super-cell architecture, for all its other real advantages (physical point-to-point wiring instead of a shared addressed bus, the whole SUPER_LATCH/core_select mechanism, everything built across `#159`-`#490`), does not yet match. Stated precisely, not as a reversal of the pivot decision: the current architecture is more flexible than the full cell in other real, concrete ways, but this SPECIFIC capability is one the pivot didn't carry forward, and it's a load-bearing one.

**Real, honest scope: nothing built, nothing scoped into concrete steps.** The natural shape of the real work this points toward -- extending the SUPER_LATCH `nano` core_config field table (or adding a genuinely new core, e.g. `branch`/`nano_full`) to carry `dynamic_route_en`/`pattern_low`/`pattern_equal`/`pattern_high` (and possibly the rest of the full nano feature set) through to `unicell_super_v1.v`'s own nano-core reconstruction, then threading that new capability up through `icm_v3.py`'s field tables, `super_tile_library_v1.py`'s own tile definitions, and from there automatically into the Tile Designer/DSL/compiler via the already-built generic registry/hook mechanisms (`#485`/`#486`) -- is a real, concrete, buildable next step, but Alan's own explicit choice was to log this now and stop, not scope or build it this session.

## 492. Real design refinement session on #491's own branch-capability gap -- a concrete shape for what "promote branching into the super cell" should look like, plus a real, second gap found in the same session while working through it (per-core watchdog wiring). Nothing built -- design captured before it drifts, per Alan's own explicit request to log it. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-25)

**Real, direct extension of #491's own `dynamic_route_en`/`pattern_low`/`pattern_equal`/`pattern_high` mechanism, not a replacement for it -- Alan's own proposal:**

**1. Mode switch, per branch/comparator cell: direction output vs. value output.** Direction mode is the existing real routing-branch idea (`#140`/`#156`), generalized. Value mode is genuinely NEW capability -- turns the same 3-way comparison into a classifier/tag generator instead of a router.

**2. Relative addressing for direction mode -- `in+1`/`in+2`/`in+3`, not absolute n/s/e/w.** A real, deliberate departure from every other direction field in the system (`downstream_mask`/`upstream_mask`/`routing_mask`/`cardinal_edge`/DSP wrapper `a_dir`/`b_dir` are all absolute compass). Offset relative to the direction data arrived FROM -- `(arrival_direction + offset) mod 4`, computed at fire time, not a static mask. Real payoff, stated by Alan directly: the exact same configured cell behaves identically no matter which side of the grid feeds it, and the 3-way outcome space (`<`/`=`/`>`) maps onto exactly the 3 non-source neighbor directions with zero wasted encoding -- deliberately kept over the absolute-mask alternative ("keep the direction idea, that's neater in someways and may prove very useful").

**3. Value mode's own further split, Alan's own refinement:** each outcome (`<`/`=`/`>`) independently selects either (a) a fixed TABLE CONSTANT (a pre-configured classification/tag code, e.g. 1/2/3), or (b) THE VALUE SUPPLIED that cycle, relayed through unchanged -- gated by outcome, not unconditional pass-through. Real, open question raised and resolved in the same session: does outcome-gated relay risk permanently stalling a branch that never satisfies its condition?

**4. The gating/stall question -- resolved, real conclusion: KEEP the option, do not curtail it.** This is the standard filter/gate idiom (alarm lines, anomaly paths, valid-flag-gated writes) -- a real, useful, foundational pattern this architecture currently has no equivalent of (every existing core either always fires when fed, or routes unconditionally, never conditionally SUPPRESSES). Explicitly distinguished from the already-known closed-relay-loop hazard (`#`-referenced finding: random topologies never quiesce, confirmed with a minimal 2-cell repro) -- that hazard is runaway, pointless ACTIVITY; outcome-gated relay dormancy is the opposite, and benign: a branch correctly staying quiet because its condition genuinely wasn't met, the same way most of a real circuit sits idle until tripped.

**5. Real, correctly-scoped hazard identified, once the gating question was pressed further:** not the gate itself, but a gated/filtered output feeding a REQUIRED MULTI-INPUT JOIN downstream with no starvation detection anywhere on that path -- narrowed directly against the real core set: only the `adder` core requires multiple arrivals (`a_arrived` AND `b_arrived`) before firing; accumulator/comparator/latch are all single-arrival-triggered and structurally can't starve this way. So the real blast radius of this hazard is small and well-defined, not systemic.

**6. The "lanes" tangent, checked directly and resolved as unrelated, not reusable, not redundant:** the only "lanes" feature in the project is `#43` ("lane-split-to-cardinals," 2026-07-19) -- FULL-cell-only (`cmd_latch`/`m_lane_cut`, the archived pre-pivot architecture), never built even there (parked, lost a bit-budget contest to `#42`), and structurally a DIFFERENT operation: UNCONDITIONAL word decomposition (every firing splits one word into byte-lanes and sends all pieces out simultaneously in a fixed cycling order) vs. this session's CONDITIONAL single-path branch (the whole value goes to exactly one place, chosen by outcome). No overlap, no reuse opportunity, and not present in the current stripped/nano/super-cell architecture at all regardless.

**7. A real, second, independent gap found while chasing "use the watchdog as the higher-level control mechanism for the join-starvation hazard" -- checked directly against the RTL, not assumed:** `watchdog_v1.v` is a real, generic, reusable module, but `grep -l "watchdog_v1" fpga/verilog/*.v` shows it is currently instantiated ONLY in the DSP wrapper family (`dsp_add_wrapper_v1.v`/`dsp_arith_wrapper_v1.v`/`dsp_compare_wrapper_v1.v`) -- never in `unicell_super_v1.v` or any individual ordinary core cell (`adder_cell_v1.v`/`accumulator_cell_v1.v`/`compare_cell_v1.v`/`latch_cell_v1.v`/`ram_cell_v1.v`). A "does a watchdog exist anywhere on this path" Designer validation rule would be near-meaningless today -- almost nothing in an ordinary design has one. This is the SAME real shape of gap `#491` already identified for branching -- real, proven hardware that was never carried from where it was built into the super shell's own core cells.

**Real, resulting dependency chain for future work, stated explicitly so it isn't attempted out of order:**
1. Build the branch/comparator mechanism itself (mode switch + relative addressing + value-mode table/relay split) -- currently just a design, nothing built.
2. Wire `watchdog_v1.v` into the ordinary super-cell cores (at minimum the `adder` core, the one real required-join point) -- the same "promote from proven-but-stranded into the super shell" work as `#491` itself, for a different piece of hardware.
3. Only once both 1 and 2 exist does a real Designer validation rule ("gated output reaches a required join with no watchdog anywhere upstream") become discriminating rather than noise -- explicitly sequenced AFTER, not built prematurely on top of a feature that doesn't exist yet.

**Real, honest scope: nothing built in this entry either, matching #491's own discipline.** This is a design session, captured in full per Alan's own explicit request ("need to run through all of that again so I have an idea of the shapes it brings up") before any of it drifts. The three-stage dependency chain above is the natural, concrete starting point whenever this gets picked back up.

## 493. Correction to #492's own three-mode framing -- the real, final shape is a per-outcome table, not three mutually-exclusive modes. Nothing built -- design only, captured before drift. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-25)

**#492 logged an intermediate framing (value mode / direction mode / gate mode, three separate modes selected once per cell) that Alan corrected in the same session -- recorded here as a real correction, not a silent edit to #492.**

**The real, final model: B (which of the 3 real comparator outcomes -- `<`/`=`/`>` -- actually happened this cycle) selects a ROW in a per-outcome table; each row independently configures three real, orthogonal fields:**
- **A -- which value:** value-in (relay the real supplied value) or fixed value (an up-to-8-bit configured constant, deliberately narrower than the comparator's existing 32-bit `threshold` to keep the field cheap).
- **C -- emit or not emit:** real, genuine suppression per outcome -- the qualitatively new capability `#492` identified (today's comparator always emits something, even a real `0`; this is true silence, not a zero value).
- **D -- direction, up to 3 (real fan-out, not single-target):** the relative `in+1`/`in+2`/`in+3` targets, and multiple can be selected at once for one outcome -- matches the EXISTING `pattern_low`/`pattern_equal`/`pattern_high` bitmask convention (`#140`) exactly, not a new precedent.

**This subsumes #492's own three modes as special cases rather than replacing them with something disjoint:** "value mode" = A=fixed for every row, D always the single legacy downstream direction; "direction mode" = A=in-value for every row, C always emitting; "gate mode" = A=in-value, D fixed, only C varying per row. The per-outcome table version lets each of the 3 outcomes do something genuinely DIFFERENT from the others in the SAME cell (e.g. `<` stays silent, `=` relays raw to `in+2`, `>` emits a fixed tag to both `in+1` and `in+3` at once) -- real conditional branching with teeth, Alan's own words, not just a config toggle.

**Real, rough bit-shape math, for later, not now:** per outcome, 1 bit (A) + 8 bits (fixed value) + 1 bit (C) + 3 bits (D, one per relative direction) = 13 bits x 3 outcomes = 39 bits, alongside the existing `threshold`/`upstream_mask` fields -- tight but plausible inside the 80-bit `SUPER_LATCH`; real budget accounting deferred to when this actually gets built, per #492's own stated three-stage dependency chain (branch mechanism -> per-core watchdog wiring -> Designer starvation-hazard validation), unchanged by this correction.

**Real, honest scope: nothing built here either.** This entry only corrects the SHAPE of the design #492 already flagged as unbuilt -- the three-stage dependency chain and "nothing built yet" status from #492 both still apply unchanged.

## 494. Resolves the open compile-time-vs-runtime question #493's own scope note raised -- in+N resolves at ICM-programming time, not baked into the .sof and not re-resolved dynamically per arrival. Nothing built -- design only. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-25)

**Alan's own reasoning, both halves of the tradeoff addressed directly:**

**Not baked into the .sof:** hardcoding which absolute direction each `in+N` means at BITSTREAM build time would fix it permanently for that specific gateware image -- too rigid, and it would mean a different physical rotation needs a full rebuild rather than just a different program.

**Not resolved dynamically at runtime either, and for a real, concrete reason:** if a branch cell's upstream could accept arrivals from more than one direction (the way today's comparator's own `upstream_mask` already allows, OR-combining multiple directions), then recomputing `in+N` fresh from WHICHEVER direction happened to deliver a given arrival would make the cell's own effective output direction non-deterministic from firing to firing -- Alan's own words, "data going every which way... if it hits it randomly." The reference direction itself would be unpredictable, so anything computed relative to it would be too.

**The real, resolved answer: ICM-programming time -- same moment every other core_config field (topology/threshold/routing_mask/etc.) already gets set.** The compiler (or the Designer, placing a tile directly) computes the real ABSOLUTE direction for each configured `in+N`, once, at placement/compile time -- because at that point the tile's own single upstream direction is already a known, fixed choice -- and bakes the resulting absolute direction bits into the core_config's own direction-table field, exactly like every other direction field already works. "Still programmable" in the sense that matters: reprogramming the ICM (without touching the .sof at all) can freely choose a different upstream direction and get a correspondingly different, still-fixed `in+N` mapping -- the .sof stays generic and reusable across any placement/orientation.

**Real, necessary consequence, now settled rather than merely flagged:** this branch/comparator core needs a SINGLE, fixed upstream direction, not a multi-direction mask like today's `comparator`'s own `upstream_mask` -- `in+N` only has one stable, well-defined meaning if there's exactly one real "in" to be relative to. This becomes a real constraint on the core's own field table when it's built (a single `upstream_dir` field, not an `upstream_mask` bitmask), not something to revisit later.

**Real, honest scope: still nothing built.** This entry resolves one open question from `#493`'s own scope note; the three-stage dependency chain from `#492` (branch mechanism -> per-core watchdog wiring -> Designer starvation-hazard validation) is unchanged.

## 497. Real, final design close-out for the branch/comparator core (#491-#494's own thread) -- the held-reference optimization that actually makes the real 42-bit `core_config` budget work, PLUS a real, separate, complementary mechanism (the shift+adder recombiner) worked out to reconstitute wide values from several narrow branch-cell outputs. Nothing built -- design only, fully settled and ready to implement. (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-25)

**Part 1 -- the held-reference optimization, closing the real `core_config` budget problem `#494` left open:**

Alan's own real insight: the comparison reference value never needs to travel through `core_config` at all. It arrives over the SAME single upstream direction every other value does, gets LATCHED and HELD indefinitely (not drained like every other single-shot core's own captured value), and every subsequent arrival is compared against the held reference rather than being captured as a new one. RELEASE (letting the held value pass through normally and clearing the latch so the next arrival becomes the new reference) is triggered by REPROGRAMMING the cell (`cfg_valid`) -- reusing a mechanism every core already has, zero new ports or control bits needed. Real sequence: program -> first arrival is captured and held as the reference (not compared, not routed) -> every later arrival is compared against it and handled per the A/C/D table -> reprogramming releases the held value (passes through normally) and the next arrival becomes the new reference.

**Real, final field table, fitting the true 42-bit `core_config` budget with room to spare:**

| Field | Width | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream_dir` | 2 bits | single fixed direction (0-3), per `#494` |
| `value_source_low/equal/high` | 1 bit each (3 total) | 0=relay the real supplied value, 1=fixed constant |
| `fixed_value_low/equal/high` | 7 bits each (21 total) | only meaningful when its own `value_source`=1 |
| `emit_low/equal/high` | 1 bit each (3 total) | real, genuine per-outcome suppression |
| `route_low/equal/high` | 4 bits each (12 total) | real absolute direction mask, RESOLVED FROM `in+1`/`in+2`/`in+3` at ICM-programming time (`#494`), real fan-out (up to 3 directions at once) |

Total: 2 + 3 + 21 + 3 + 12 = **41 bits**, one spare bit inside the real 42-bit budget. `threshold` is GONE as a config field entirely -- it's runtime state now (the held-reference register), not configuration.

**Real, honest scope: this closes the field-layout question definitively.** RTL (`branch_cell_v1.v`), VM dispatch, `icm_v3.py`/`root_definition.json` field table entries, and `super_tile_library_v1.py`'s own tile registration are the concrete next real steps whenever this gets built -- not done in this entry.

**Part 2 -- the recombiner: a real, SEPARATE, complementary mechanism, needing ZERO new RTL.**

Real motivation: `fixed_value` above is only 7 bits, a genuine precision cost the held-reference design accepted. The recombiner reconstitutes a wider composite word from several narrow branch-cell outputs -- but per Alan's own real, correct observation, it doesn't manufacture entropy, only repackages what already went in (a single branch cell round-robining into it gives a degenerate repeated-code pattern; four independent branch cells give a real but bounded `2^28`, not the full `2^32`, distinct-output space). Real, honest design note captured for future reference: the recombiner is for reconstituting several independent narrow CLASSIFICATIONS into one composite word -- it is NOT the tool for preserving a single arbitrary 32-bit value untouched. That case is already covered directly by the branch cell's own relay mode (`value_source`=0), which never touches the narrow field at all.

**Real, working construction, using cells this project has ALREADY built and proven, not new hardware:** each real byte is `(7 real bits + 1 zero pad)` = 8 bits, matching a real, already-supported discrete shift amount in `shift_lane_addon_v1.v` ({1,2,4,8,12,16,20,24,28} -- 8 is directly in that set, confirmed, not assumed). Because the running accumulator occupies strictly higher bit positions than the freshly-arriving byte at every fold (no bit position ever overlaps), ADDITION and OR are mathematically identical here -- no carry can ever occur -- so the existing `adder_cell_v1.v` performs the real combine step correctly with zero modification. Building a full 32-bit word from 4 real bytes needs 3 folds, each fold = one shift-relay cell (shift_lane_addon, amount=8) + one adder cell = 6 extra cells total for the whole chain, on top of whichever branch cells produce the 4 raw bytes.

**Real, deliberate sequencing decision, Alan's own call:** build the recombiner as a real, composable MULTI-CELL PATTERN first (matching this whole system's own "Lego" philosophy directly, Alan's own words) rather than investing in a dedicated single-cycle packer core -- real, already-proven cells, zero new RTL/sim/hardware-proving burden, at the real cost of more cells and 3 real cycles (one per fold) instead of one. A dedicated packer core remains a real, legitimate future option if cell/real-estate cost ever actually matters for this pattern once it's used for real -- not built now, not needed now.

**Real, honest question, sent to Alan, not yet independently confirmed:** whether the fold operation is a FIXED shift-by-8 applied identically at every stage (accumulator repeatedly shifted left 8, fresh byte OR'd in at the bottom each time -- `((((V1<<8|V2)<<8|V3)<<8|V4))`, which lets all three fold stages be literally identical cell configurations reused), or a GROWING shift amount per stage (8, then 16, then 24). The fixed-shift reading is assumed correct (matches Alan's own "position 0 -> 8 -> 16" description read as describing where the accumulated block ends up after each successive fixed-8 fold, not literal escalating shift instructions) but stated honestly as the working assumption, not independently reconfirmed word-for-word.

## 498. Real, foundational architecture principle stated explicitly by Alan, logged before drift, plus two real documentation deliverables built to carry it forward: `docs/stripped-cell/CELL_GOTCHAS.md` (new) and a real extension to `CORES_AND_WRAPPERS_REFERENCE.md` covering standalone-vs-super-carrier behavior (#477's own original, unstarted ask). (Alan/Claude, 2026-08-25)

**The real, governing principle, Alan's own words, precisely: prefer a CORE over a specialist/dedicated cell.** A new CORE joins `unicell_super_v1.v`'s own `core_select` mux -- every cell in the grid can become it, chosen freely at ICM-programming time, so any structure built from it can be placed ANYWHERE and rearranged by a different ICM program with zero `.sof` rebuild. A specialist cell (the DSP wrapper family's own real category) is wired into fixed grid positions at `.sof`-build time -- permanent for that bitstream. Building specialist cells by default would progressively fix more of the grid's own layout at synthesis time, eroding the real mutability the whole ICM/Designer/compiler stack depends on -- "any structure can be anywhere, not fixed in a `.sof` design," Alan's own words, now captured verbatim rather than paraphrased into something weaker.

**The real, known exception, not a contradiction:** genuinely scarce, expensive hard-IP-adjacent resources -- the DSP wrapper family's own already-stated real reason for existing outside `core_select` (`#453`/`#474`): making Nios custom-instruction floating-point hardware universal would tax every cell's own ALM budget whether it's used or not. Specialist placement is correct when the underlying resource genuinely can't be cheaply replicated everywhere -- the exception, not the default.

**Real, concrete proof the DEFAULT (prefer cores/composition) actually works, found earlier the SAME session, now explicitly connected to this principle:** the recombiner (`#497`) is built entirely from two things that are ALREADY universal -- `adder_cell_v1.v` and `shift_lane_addon_v1.v` -- rather than as a new dedicated packer cell. Real capability, zero new position-fixed hardware, exactly the shape this principle asks for.

**Real documentation work, both requested directly, matching #477's own original, long-unstarted ask (\"the real difference in behavior/role between a module used STANDALONE versus the SAME module used as a CORE inside the super carrier shell\"):**

1. **`docs/stripped-cell/CORES_AND_WRAPPERS_REFERENCE.md` extended** with two new real sections: the design principle above (with its real, stated exception), and a real, CHECKED (not assumed) standalone-vs-super-carrier behavior summary -- five of the six cores (RAM/adder/accumulator/comparator/latch) behave IDENTICALLY in both contexts, confirmed directly against `unicell_super_automaton_v1.py`'s own dispatch code, no reduced field set anywhere. Nano is the ONE real exception (the already-known `#490`/`#491` gap), now stated in this reference doc directly rather than only living in `points.md` history -- and explicitly connected as the real reason the branch/comparator core exists at all: a new, universal core built to bring nano's own stranded capability class into the super shell properly, per the design principle, rather than patching nano's own reduced subset piecemeal.

2. **New `docs/stripped-cell/CELL_GOTCHAS.md`** -- a real, dedicated reference for a different kind of fact than either existing doc covers: not \"what exists\" (`CORES_AND_WRAPPERS_REFERENCE.md`), not \"how was this proven\" (`points.md`), but \"what do you have to already know about THIS cell/mechanism or you will not get the correct working result, even though nothing looks wrong.\" Splits gotchas into two real, differently-fixed categories: WIRING/STRUCTURAL ones (the real fix is a composed tile that enforces the structure, not a note describing it) and SINGLE-CELL BEHAVIORAL ones (no composed tile can fix these; the only real fix is knowing the fact). Seeded with everything already real and settled this session: the branch cell's held-reference release mechanism and its single-fixed-upstream-direction constraint, the recombiner's exact required wiring and its honest entropy limitation, the DSP watchdog's sim-vs-real-JTAG timescale mismatch, per-DSP-operation hardware-confirmation status, the DSP entity-naming lesson (top-level name vs. internal Qsys kind), and nano's own standalone-vs-super-carrier gap.

**Real, honest scope, both docs marked for ongoing maintenance, not treated as a one-time snapshot:** `CELL_GOTCHAS.md` explicitly notes its one currently-open action item (register a real `recombiner_4way` composed tile once the branch cell itself is built, so the recombiner's own structural requirement is enforced by the tile system instead of only being described in a doc) -- matching the principle from earlier in this same entry: a composed tile is the real fix for a structural gotcha, a doc is only the fallback for what a composed tile can't cover.
